title: Counter-UAS & Base Defense
attribution: Mokuhyo contributors. English definitions: US Government works (public domain) — DoD Dictionary, ATP 3-01.81, JP 3-10, JP 3-01, ATP 1-02.1 — or original where marked. Target-language terms aligned with the allied sources cited per term; definitions, examples and dialogues AI-drafted with Mistral-Small-3.2-24B, pending human review.

terms.definitionEn: That system of equipment, network, and personnel to control an unmanned aircraft. Also called UAS.
terms.definition: 무인기체계는 무인항공기를 제어하기 위한 장비, 네트워크, 그리고 인원으로 구성된 시스템입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports for formal communication.

examples.text: 무인기체계가 목표 지점 주변에서 정찰 중입니다.
examples.english: The unmanned aircraft system is conducting reconnaissance around the target area.
The unmanned aircraft system was successfully launched.

terms.definitionEn: An aircraft that does not carry a human operator and is capable of flight with or without human remote control. Also called UA.
terms.definition: 무인항공기는 인간 조종사가 탑승하지 않고, 원격 조종이 가능하거나 불가능한 비행이 가능한 항공기입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.english: The unmanned aircraft is flying at low altitude.

examples.text: 무인항공기가 목표 지점을 향해 이동 중입니다.
examples.english: The unmanned aircraft is moving towards the target.

terms.definitionEn: An unmanned aircraft system whose aircraft weighs less than 55 pounds, together with its ground control station and data links.
terms.definition: 소형무인항공기체계는 항공기가 55파운드 미만인 무인항공기 시스템으로, 지상 제어소와 데이터 링크가 포함됩니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports for formal communication.

examples.english: The small unmanned aircraft system is conducting reconnaissance inside the building.
The small unmanned aircraft system landed successfully.

terms.definitionEn: One of five size classes the US military uses for unmanned aircraft, from Group 1 (under 20 pounds, low and slow) to Group 5 (over 1,320 pounds, flying above 18,000 feet).
terms.definition: 무인항공기그룹은 미국 군대가 무인항공기를 20파운드 미만부터 1,320파운드 초과까지 5개의 크기 그룹으로 분류한 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports for formal communication.

examples.english: UAS Group 3 operates at medium altitude.

examples.text: 무인항공기그룹 5는 장기간 정찰 임무를 수행할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: UAS Group 5 can perform long-endurance reconnaissance missions.

terms.definitionEn: A small drone flown by an operator who watches a live video feed from its onboard camera, often through goggles, and often used as a guided explosive weapon.
terms.definition: FPV 드론은 조종사가 드론의 온보드 카메라에서 실시간 영상을 통해 조종하는 소형 드론으로, 종종 폭발성 무기로 사용됩니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.text: FPV 드론이 목표 지점을 향해 비행 중입니다.
examples.english: The FPV drone is flying towards the target.
The FPV drone detonated successfully.

terms.definitionEn: Loitering munition is a reference to any UAS that can engage beyond line-of-sight ground targets with an explosive warhead or lethal payload to cause injury via a “suicide mode” attack. 1-8.
terms.definition: 유도무기는 목표를 추적하고 폭발성 유탄이나 치명적인 화물을 탑재하여 "자살 모드" 공격으로 지상 목표를 공격할 수 있는 UAS를 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.text: 유도무기가 목표 지점을 향해 비행 중입니다.
examples.english: The loitering munition is flying towards the target.
The loitering munition detonated successfully.

terms.definitionEn: A group of unmanned aircraft that operate together under coordinated or automated control to overwhelm defenses or complete a shared task.
terms.definition: 무인항공기집단은 조정되거나 자동화된 제어 하에 함께 작동하는 무인항공기 그룹으로, 방어선을 압도하거나 공유 작업을 완료하는 데 사용됩니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports for formal communication.

examples.text: 무인항공기집단이 목표 지점을 향해 이동 중입니다.
examples.english: The swarm of unmanned aircraft is moving towards the target.
The swarm of unmanned aircraft successfully attacked the target.

terms.definitionEn: An aircraft that gets lift from wings that do not move, so it must keep moving forward to stay in the air.
terms.definition: 고정익항공기는 고정된 날개에서 상승력을 얻기 때문에 공중을 유지하기 위해 계속 앞으로 이동해야 하는 항공기입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.text: 고정익항공기가 목표 지점을 향해 비행 중입니다.
examples.english: The fixed-wing aircraft is flying towards the target.
The fixed-wing aircraft landed successfully.

terms.definitionEn: An aircraft that gets lift from spinning rotor blades, so it can take off vertically and hover.
terms.definition: 회전익항공기는 회전하는 로터 날개에서 상승력을 얻기 때문에 수직으로 이륙하고 호버링할 수 있는 항공기입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.text: 회전익항공기가 목표 지점을 향해 비행 중입니다.
examples.english: The rotary-wing aircraft is flying towards the target.
The rotary-wing aircraft landed successfully.

terms.definitionEn: A drone lifted by several horizontal propellers (commonly four, six or eight) that lets it hover and change direction quickly.
terms.definition: 멀티로터드론은 여러 수평 프로펠러(보통 4, 6, 또는 8개)에 의해 들어올려져 빠르게 호버링하고 방향을 바꿀 수 있는 드론입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and reports.

examples.text: 멀티로터드론이 목표 지점을 향해 비행 중입니다.
examples.english: The multirotor drone is flying towards the target.
The multirotor drone landed successfully.

terms.definitionEn: The equipment, people and procedures used to detect, track, identify and defeat hostile or unauthorized unmanned aircraft.
terms.definition: 무인항공기방어체계는 적대적이거나 허가되지 않은 무인항공기를 탐지, 추적, 식별하고 격퇴하기 위한 장비, 인력, 절차의 조합입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.text: 무인항공기방어체계가 작동 중입니다. 모든 부대는 경계를 강화하세요.
examples.english: The counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) is operational. All units, enhance your security.
The C-UAS has detected a drone. Respond immediately.

terms.definitionEn: A defense that places several sensors and weapons at different ranges so that a threat that gets past one layer can still be stopped by the next.
terms.definition: 다층방어는 여러 센서와 무기를 다른 거리에서 배치하여 위협이 한 층을 통과하더라도 다음 층에서 막을 수 있도록 하는 방어 시스템입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.english: The layered defense system has blocked a drone intrusion.
Strengthen the layered defense to block all access routes.

terms.definitionEn: In counter-UAS, the first step: sensing that an aircraft or drone is present, by radar, radio-frequency, optical or acoustic sensors.
terms.definition: 탐지는 레이더, 무선주파수, 광학 또는 음향 센서를 사용하여 항공기 또는 드론이 존재함을 감지하는 첫 번째 단계입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 탐지가 완료되었습니다. 무인기가 5km 떨어진 곳에 있습니다.
examples.english: Detection complete. A drone is 5km away.
The detection system has picked up a drone's signal.

terms.definitionEn: Precise and continuous position-finding of targets by radar, optical, or other means.
terms.definition: 추적은 레이더, 광학 또는 기타 수단을 사용하여 표적의 정확하고 연속적인 위치를 찾는 과정입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 추적이 시작되었습니다. 무인기의 위치는 계속 업데이트됩니다.
examples.english: Tracking has begun. The drone's position is being continuously updated.
The tracking system is following the drone's path.

terms.definitionEn: 1. The process of determining the friendly or hostile character of an unknown detected contact. 2. In arms control, the process of determining which nation is responsible for the detected violations of any arms control measure. 3. In ground combat operations, discrimination between recognizable objects as being friendly or enemy, or the name that belongs to the object as a member of a class. Also called ID.
terms.definition: 식별은 탐지된 접촉의 우호적이거나 적대적인 성격을 결정하는 과정입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: Identification complete. The drone is hostile.

examples.text: 식별 프로세스가 진행 중입니다. 잠시만 기다리세요.
examples.english: The identification process is underway. Please wait a moment.

terms.definitionEn: In counter-UAS, the step that stops an unmanned aircraft from completing its mission, by destroying it, disabling it or taking control of it.
terms.definition: 무인기 격퇴는 무인항공기를 파괴하거나 무력화하거나 제어하여 그 임무를 완수하지 못하도록 하는 단계입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: Drone defeat successful. The threat has been neutralized.
Launch a missile to defeat the drone.

terms.definitionEn: Stopping an unmanned aircraft by physically hitting it, for example with gunfire, a missile, an interceptor drone or a net.
terms.definition: 운동에너지 격퇴는 총격, 미사일, 요격 드론 또는 그물과 같은 방법으로 무인항공기를 물리적으로 충돌시켜 막는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.text: 운동에너지 격퇴가 효과적입니다. 모든 부대는 대응을 준비하세요.
examples.english: Kinetic defeat is effective. All units, prepare to respond.
The kinetic defeat system has shot down the drone.

terms.definitionEn: Stopping an unmanned aircraft without physically hitting it, for example by jamming its control link or its satellite navigation.
terms.definition: 비운동에너지 격퇴는 제어 링크 또는 위성 항법 시스템을 방해하는 등 물리적으로 충돌하지 않고 무인항공기를 막는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.text: 비운동에너지 격퇴가 성공했습니다. 무인기의 제어 시스템이 마비되었습니다.
examples.english: Non-kinetic defeat successful. The drone's control system is disabled.

examples.text: 비운동에너지 격퇴를 위해 전자전 장비를 사용하세요.
examples.english: Use electronic warfare equipment for non-kinetic defeat.

terms.definitionEn: Finding a drone by picking up the radio signals passing between it and its controller, which can also point to where the operator is.
terms.definition: 무선주파수(RF) 탐지는 드론과 그 조종자 사이의 무선 신호를 포착하여 드론을 찾고 조종자의 위치를 추적하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: RF detection has picked up the drone's signal.
The RF detection system is operational.

terms.definitionEn: A sensor that sends out radio waves and measures their echoes to find the position, speed and direction of objects such as aircraft.
terms.definition: 레이더는 항공기와 같은 물체의 위치를, 속도 및 방향을 측정하기 위해 무선파를 발사하고 그 반사파를 측정하는 센서입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: Radar has detected the drone. Its position is confirmed.

examples.text: 레이더 시스템이 무인기의 속도와 방향을 추적 중입니다.
examples.english: The radar system is tracking the drone's speed and direction.

terms.definitionEn: A camera system that uses visible light and heat images to see, follow and identify a target by day or night.
terms.definition: 전자광학/적외선(EO/IR) 센서는 가시광선과 열화상을 사용하여 낮과 밤에 표적을 감시하고 식별하는 카메라 시스템입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in technical reports and briefings.

examples.text: EO/IR 센서가 표적의 위치를 실시간으로 추적하고 있습니다.
examples.english: The EO/IR sensor is tracking the target's location in real time.
We have detected the enemy's drone using the EO/IR sensor.

terms.definitionEn: A sensor that detects a drone by listening for the sound of its motors and propellers.
terms.definition: 음향 센서는 드론의 모터와 프로펠러 소음을 감지하여 드론을 탐지하는 센서입니다.
terms.registerNote: Common in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 음향 센서가 드론의 엔진 소음을 감지했습니다.
examples.english: The acoustic sensor has detected the drone's engine noise.

examples.text: 저고도 비행하는 드론을 음향 센서로 식별했습니다.
examples.english: We have identified the low-flying drone using the acoustic sensor.

terms.definitionEn: The employment of limited offensive action and counterattacks to deny a contested area or position to the enemy.
terms.definition: 적극적 방어는 적에게 특정 지역이나 위치를 허용하지 않기 위해 제한적인 공격과 반격을 수행하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in strategic planning and briefings.

examples.text: 적극적 방어 작전을 통해 적의 공세를 차단했습니다.
examples.english: We have blocked the enemy's offensive with active defense operations.

examples.text: 전초 기지에서 적극적 방어 태세를 유지하겠습니다.
examples.english: We will maintain an active defense posture at the outpost.

terms.definitionEn: Measures taken to reduce the probability of and to minimize the effects of damage caused by hostile action without the intention of taking the initiative.
terms.definition: 수동적 방어는 적의 공격 효과를 최소화하기 위해 취하는 조치로, 공격적인 행동의 의도가 없습니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal register.

examples.text: 수동적 방어 시스템이 적의 공격으로 인한 피해를 최소화합니다.
examples.english: The passive defense system minimizes damage from enemy attacks.

examples.text: 수동적 방어 전략은 우리의 방어력을 높입니다.
examples.english: The passive defense strategy enhances our defensive capabilities.

terms.definitionEn: The deliberate radiation, reradiation, or reflection of electromagnetic energy for the purpose of preventing or reducing the effective use of the electromagnetic spectrum, with the intent of degrading or disrupting combat capability.
terms.definition: 전자기파 교란은 적의 전자기파 사용을 방해하거나 저하시키기 위해 전자기파를 의도적으로 방사, 재방사, 또는 반사하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and tactical reports.

examples.text: 전자기파 교란 장치를 가동하여 적의 통신을 차단했습니다.
examples.english: We have activated the electromagnetic jamming device to block the enemy's communications.

examples.text: 교란 장치로 인해 적의 레이더가 마비되었습니다.
examples.english: The enemy's radar has been paralyzed due to the jamming device.

terms.definitionEn: Sending false signals, such as fake satellite navigation data, so that a drone or receiver believes it is somewhere it is not.
terms.definition: 스푸핑은 가짜 위성항법 데이터를 보내어 드론이나 수신기가 실제 위치가 아닌 다른 위치로 인식하도록 하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Common in technical discussions and reports.

examples.text: 스푸핑 공격으로 적의 드론이 잘못된 위치로 유도되었습니다.
examples.english: The enemy's drone was misled to a wrong location due to a spoofing attack.

examples.text: 스푸핑 기술로 적의 GPS 신호를 왜곡했습니다.
examples.english: We have distorted the enemy's GPS signal using spoofing technology.

terms.definitionEn: Actions taken to maintain friendly use of positioning, navigation, and timing information while denying the same to an adversary. Also called NAVWAR.
terms.definition: 항법전은 친군의 위치, 항법, 시간 정보를 유지하면서 적에게는 이를 거부하는 조치를 취하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in strategic planning and briefings.

examples.text: 항법전 작전으로 인해 적의 위성 내비게이션이 교란되었습니다.
examples.english: The enemy's satellite navigation has been jammed due to navigation warfare operations.

examples.text: 항법전 태세를 강화하여 우리군의 정확한 위치 파악이 가능합니다.
examples.english: We can accurately determine our military's position by strengthening the navigation warfare posture.

terms.definitionEn: The production of a beam of concentrated electromagnetic energy or atomic or subatomic particles. Also called DE.
terms.definition: 유도 에너지란 집중된 전자기파 또는 원자 또는 하전입자의 빔을 생성하는 것을 말합니다.
terms.registerNote: Found in technical reports and briefings.

examples.english: Directed energy weapons are being developed.

examples.text: 유도 에너지를 이용한 신무기 실험이 성공적으로 진행되었습니다.
examples.english: The experiment of new weapons using directed energy was successfully conducted.

terms.definitionEn: A weapon or system that uses directed energy to incapacitate, damage, or destroy enemy equipment, facilities, and/or personnel.
terms.definition: 유도 에너지 무기는 집중된 에너지를 사용하여 적의 장비, 시설 또는 인원을 무력화, 손상, 또는 파괴하는 무기입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in tactical reports and briefings.

examples.text: 유도 에너지 무기로 적의 드론을 격파했습니다.
examples.english: We have shot down the enemy's drone using a directed-energy weapon.

examples.text: 유도 에너지 무기의 정밀도로 인해 적의 장비에 치명적인 피해를 입혔습니다.
examples.english: Due to the precision of directed energy weapons, we have inflicted fatal damage on the enemy's equipment.

terms.definitionEn: A drone launched to chase and destroy or capture a hostile drone in the air.
terms.definition: 요격 드론은 공중에서 적의 드론을 추적하여 파괴하거나 포획하기 위해 발사되는 드론입니다.
terms.registerNote: Common in radio communications and tactical reports.

examples.text: 요격 드론이 적의 무인기에게 접근 중입니다.
examples.english: The interceptor drone is approaching the enemy's UAV.

examples.text: 요격 드론이 적의 드론을 성공적으로 격추시켰습니다.
examples.english: The interceptor drone has successfully shot down the enemy's drone.

terms.definitionEn: Defeating a small drone by catching it in a net fired from the ground or carried by another drone.
terms.definition: 작은 드론을 땅에서 발사하거나 다른 드론이 운반하는 그물로 포획하여 무력화하는 것
terms.registerNote: Used in written reports and briefings.

examples.text: 네트 포획을 사용하여 적의 소형 무인기를 격파하라.
examples.english: Use net capture to defeat the enemy's small drone.

examples.text: 목표 지점에서 네트 포획을 준비하고, 적의 무인기가 접근하면 즉시 발사하라.
examples.english: Prepare for net capture at the target point, and fire immediately when the enemy drone approaches.

terms.definitionEn: The radio connection over which an operator sends commands to an unmanned aircraft and receives its status.
terms.definition: 조종사가 무인 항공기에 명령을 보내고 그 상태를 받는 무선 연결
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and training materials.

examples.text: C2 링크가 끊어지면, 즉시 예비 시스템으로 전환하라.
examples.english: If the C2 link is lost, immediately switch to the backup system.

examples.text: 조종사는 C2 링크를 통해 무인기의 상태를 모니터링하고 명령하라.
examples.english: The operator should monitor the drone's status and issue commands via the C2 link.

terms.definitionEn: A radio connection that passes data, such as video, position and commands, between an aircraft and the ground or other units.
terms.definition: 항공기와 지상 또는 다른 부대 사이에 비디오, 위치 및 명령과 같은 데이터를 전달하는 무선 연결
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 데이터 링크로 실시간 영상을 수신 중입니다.
examples.english: Receiving real-time video via data link.

examples.text: 데이터 링크가 불안정하면, 즉시 기술 지원팀에 연락하라.
examples.english: If the data link is unstable, contact the technical support team immediately.

terms.definitionEn: A range of radio frequencies; many small drones use the 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands for control and video.
terms.definition: 무선 주파수의 범위; 많은 소형 드론은 제어 및 비디오에 2.4 GHz 및 5.8 GHz 대역을 사용
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and technical reports.

examples.english: Please check the frequency band.

examples.text: 주파수 대역이 일치하지 않아 연결이 안 됩니다.
examples.english: The connection fails because the frequency bands do not match.

terms.definitionEn: A drone's broadcast of its identity, location and the location of its control station, which receivers on the ground can read.
terms.definition: 드론이 자신의 신원, 위치 및 제어 기지의 위치를 방송하여 지상 수신기가 읽을 수 있는 시스템
terms.registerNote: Used in written reports and standard operating procedures.

examples.text: 원격 식별 신호를 수신하여 무인기의 위치를 확인하라.
examples.english: Confirm the drone's location by receiving Remote ID signals.

examples.text: 모든 무인기는 원격 식별 기능을 탑재해야 합니다.
examples.english: All drones must be equipped with Remote ID functionality.

terms.definitionEn: The place from which a person is controlling a drone; finding it lets security forces stop the threat at its source.
terms.definition: 사람이 드론을 조종하는 장소; 이를 찾으면 보안 요원이 위협의 근원을 차단할 수 있음
terms.registerNote: Used in intelligence reports and briefings.

examples.text: 드론 조종자 위치를 파악하면, 위협의 근원을 차단할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Finding the drone operator location lets you stop the threat at its source.

examples.text: 조종자 위치를 추적하기 위해 추가 자료를 요청하라.
examples.english: Request additional information to track the operator's location.

terms.definitionEn: The place from which an unmanned aircraft takes off.
terms.definition: 무인 항공기가 이륙하는 장소
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 적의 발사 지점을 확인하고, 즉시 대응하라.
examples.english: Confirm the enemy's launch point and respond immediately.

examples.text: 무인기의 발사 지점을 파악하기 위해 정찰기를 파견하라.
examples.english: Dispatch a reconnaissance aircraft to identify the drone's launch point.

terms.definitionEn: The place where an unmanned aircraft is planned to land or be collected after its flight.
terms.definition: 무인 항공기가 비행 후 착륙하거나 회수될 예정인 장소
terms.registerNote: Used in mission planning and briefings.

examples.text: 회수 지점을 설정하고, 무인기의 안전한 회수를 보장하라.
examples.english: Set the recovery point and ensure the safe recovery of the drone.

examples.text: 무인기의 회수 지점을 확인하고, 필요한 경우 지원하라.
examples.english: Confirm the drone's recovery point and provide support if necessary.

terms.definitionEn: The planned or observed path of an aircraft in altitude, speed and direction over time.
terms.definition: 항공기가 시간별로 고도, 속도 및 방향을 따라가는 계획 또는 관찰된 경로
terms.registerNote: Used in intelligence reports and briefings.

examples.text: 무인기의 비행 프로파일을 분석하여 적의 의도를 파악하라.
examples.english: Analyze the drone's flight profile to understand the enemy's intentions.

examples.text: 비행 프로파일을 기반으로 무인기의 이동 경로를 예측하라.
examples.english: Predict the drone's movement path based on its flight profile.

terms.definitionEn: To stay over or near an area for a period of time, for example to watch it or to wait for a target.
terms.definition: 특정 지역을 관찰하거나 표적을 기다리기 위해 일정 기간 동안 그 위치를 유지하는 것
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and mission planning.

examples.text: 무인기는 목표 지점에서 정지 비행하며 상황을 모니터링하라.
examples.english: The drone should loiter over the target point and monitor the situation.

examples.text: 정지 비행 중인 무인기에 대해 추가 지시를 내릴 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Additional instructions can be given to the drone while it is loitering.

terms.definitionEn: The movement of an aircraft into an area toward its target or objective.
terms.definition: 항공기가 목표나 임무 지역으로 이동하는 것
terms.registerNote: Used in radio and written reports for aircraft movement.

examples.english: The aircraft is in ingress to the target.

examples.text: 적 전투기들이 우리의 방공 식별 구역에 진입하고 있습니다.
examples.english: Enemy fighters are ingressing our air defense identification zone.

terms.definitionEn: The movement of an aircraft out of a target area after completing its task.
terms.definition: 항공기가 임무를 완료한 후 목표 지역을 떠나는 것
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and mission briefings.

examples.english: Egress immediately after completing the mission.
The fighter is egressing the target area.

terms.definitionEn: An attack by many aircraft, drones or missiles arriving at the same time to overload the defenses.
terms.definition: 많은 항공기, 드론 또는 미사일이 동시에 도착하여 방어 시스템을 과부하 상태로 만드는 공격
terms.registerNote: Used in strategic planning and mission reports.

examples.english: Neutralize the enemy's defense with a mass raid.

examples.text: 여러 대의 무인기들이 대량 공습을 위해 접근 중입니다.
examples.english: Multiple drones are approaching for a mass raid.

terms.definitionEn: The point at which more threats arrive than the defense can detect, track or engage at once.
terms.definition: 방어 시스템이 감지, 추적 또는 동시에 대응할 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 위협이 도착하는 지점
terms.registerNote: Used in tactical assessments and radio communication.

examples.text: 포화 상태에서 추가 목표를 처리할 수 없습니다.
examples.english: Cannot engage additional targets in saturation.
The enemy's saturation has overwhelmed our defense.

terms.definitionEn: A form of collateral effect that causes unintentional or incidental injury or damage to persons or objects that would not be lawful military targets in the circumstances ruling at the time.
terms.definition: 합법적인 군사 목표가 아닌 대상을 우발적으로 손상시키는 부수적 결과
terms.registerNote: Used in mission debriefs and damage assessments.

examples.english: Minimize collateral damage during the operation.
Collateral damage from the airstrike has been reported.

terms.definitionEn: A defined airspace in which a particular weapon system engages air and missile threats. Also called WEZ.
terms.definition: 특정 무기 시스템이 공중 및 미사일 위협을 공격하는 정해진 항공 공간
terms.registerNote: Used in mission briefings and radio communication.

examples.english: Engage targets only within the WEZ.
We shot down an enemy fighter in the designated WEZ.

terms.definitionEn: An air and missile defense control measure declared for a particular area and time by an area air defense commander, or delegated subordinate commander, based on the rules of engagement that establish the conditions under which fighters and surface air defense weapons are permitted to engage threats. Also call WCS.
terms.definition: 특정 지역과 시간에 대한 공중 및 미사일 방어 조종 조치로, 전투기 및 지상 방공 무기가 위협을 공격할 수 있는 조건을 설정
terms.registerNote: Used in command and control communication.

examples.english: Weapons control status changed to weapons free.
Current weapons control status is weapons tight.

terms.definitionEn: Weapons free is the least restrictive status: used to indicate when any target not positively identified as friendly in accordance with current ROE may be engaged.
terms.definition: 현재 규칙에 따라 우호적으로 확인되지 않은 모든 목표를 공격할 수 있는 가장 제한이 적은 상태
terms.registerNote: Used in command and control communication.

examples.english: Shot down an enemy fighter in weapons free status.
Engage targets in weapons free status.

terms.definitionEn: Weapons tight is the normal status. Units may only fire on targets identified as hostile in accordance with current ROE.
terms.definition: 현재 규칙에 따라 적대적으로 확인된 목표만 공격할 수 있는 정상 상태
terms.registerNote: Used in command and control communication.

examples.english: Engage targets only in weapons tight status.
Confirmed an enemy fighter in weapons tight status.

terms.definitionEn: Weapons hold is the most restrictive status. Units may only fire in self-defense or when ordered by proper higher authority.
terms.definition: 적대적으로 확인된 목표만 공격할 수 있는 가장 제한이 많은 상태
terms.registerNote: Used in command and control communication.

examples.english: Fire only in self-defense in weapons hold status.
Detected an enemy fighter in weapons hold status.

terms.definitionEn: Directives issued by competent military authority that delineate the circumstances and limitations under which United States forces will initiate and/or continue combat engagement with other forces encountered. Also called ROE.
terms.definition: 작전지침은 미국 군대가 전투에 참여할 수 있는 조건과 한계를 명확히 하는 지침입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, always formal.

examples.text: 작전지침은 반드시 준수해야 합니다. 모든 병력은 이 지침을 이해하고 따라야 합니다.
examples.english: The rules of engagement must be strictly followed. All personnel must understand and comply with these directives.

examples.text: 작전지침에 따라 행동하세요. 적대행위를 예방하기 위해 신중하게 판단해야 합니다.
examples.english: Act according to the rules of engagement. You must carefully judge to prevent hostile acts.

terms.definitionEn: The use of force or other attack against the United States, United States forces, or other designated persons or property to preclude or impede the mission and/or duties of United States forces, including the recovery of United States personnel or vital United States Government property.
terms.definition: 적대행위는 미국 군대의 임무 수행을 방해하거나 막기 위해 사용되는 힘이나 공격 행위를 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports, formal.

examples.english: Report immediately upon detecting any hostile act.
Respond according to the rules of engagement when a hostile act is confirmed.

terms.definitionEn: The threat of imminent use of force against the United States, United States forces, or other designated persons or property.
terms.definition: 적대의도는 미국이나 미국 군대에 대한 즉각적인 힘의 사용 위협을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.text: 적대의도 감지 시 경고하고 대응 태세를 취하세요.
examples.english: Warn and assume response posture upon detecting hostile intent.
Report to higher command immediately when hostile intent is confirmed.

terms.definitionEn: An identification derived from observation and analysis of target characteristics, including visual recognition; electronic support systems; non-cooperative target recognition techniques; identification, friend or foe systems; or other physicsbased identification techniques. Also called PID.
terms.definition: 확인식식별은 시각 인식, 전자 지원 시스템, 비협력적 표적 인식 기술 등을 통해 표적의 특성을 관찰하고 분석하여 도출되는 식별 방법입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.english: Analyze enemy characteristics for positive identification.

examples.text: 확인식식별이 완료되면 목표에 대한 조치를 취하세요.
examples.english: Take action against the target once positive identification is complete.

terms.definitionEn: The number assigned to an air track so that everyone in the air defense system refers to the same object.
terms.definition: 추적번호는 항공 추적에 할당되는 번호로, 모든 공중 방어 시스템이 동일한 객체를 참조할 수 있도록 합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports, formal.

examples.text: 추적번호 1234는 적기입니다. 모든 부대는 이 추적번호를 모니터링하세요.
examples.english: Track number 1234 is an enemy aircraft. All units monitor this track number.

examples.text: 추적번호 5678는 친구입니다. 조종사는 이 추적번호를 확인하세요.
examples.english: Track number 5678 is friendly. Pilots confirm this track number.

terms.definitionEn: 1. A series of related contacts displayed on a data display console or other display device. 2. To display or record the successive positions of a moving object. 3. To lock onto a point of radiation and obtain guidance therefrom. 4. To keep a gun properly aimed or to point a target-locating instrument continuously at a moving target. 5. The actual path of an aircraft above or a ship on the surface of the Earth. 6. One of the two endless belts on which a full-track or half-track vehicle runs. 7. A metal part forming a path for a moving object such as the track around the inside of a vehicle for moving a mounted machine gun.
terms.definition: 추적은 데이터 표시 콘솔이나 다른 표시 장치에 표시되는 관련 접촉의 시리즈입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and briefings, formal.

examples.english: Begin tracking. Observe the enemy aircraft's movements.

examples.text: 추적을 계속하세요. 모든 데이터는 기록되야 합니다.
examples.english: Continue tracking. All data must be recorded.

terms.definitionEn: A single, identical display of relevant information shared by more than one command that facilitates collaborative planning and assists all echelons to achieve situational awareness. Also called COP.
terms.definition: 공동작전상황도는 여러 명령이 공유하는 동일한 관련 정보 표시로, 협력적 계획 수립을 용이하게 하고 모든 단계에서 상황 인식을 돕습니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.text: 공동작전상황도를 보세요. 모든 부대는 같은 정보를 공유하고 있습니다.
examples.english: View the common operational picture. All units share the same information.
Plan based on the common operational picture.

terms.definitionEn: Measures employed to facilitate the efficient use of airspace to accomplish missions and simultaneously provide safeguards for friendly forces. Also called ACMs.
terms.definition: 항공공간조정조치는 임무 수행을 효율적으로 수행하고 동시에 우방 군대를 보호하기 위해 항공 공간을 효율적으로 사용하기 위해 취해진 조치입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.text: 항공공간조정조치를 준수하세요. 항공기 간 충돌을 방지하세요.
examples.english: Comply with airspace coordinating measures. Prevent aircraft collisions.
Adjust flight paths according to airspace coordinating measures.

terms.definitionEn: Airspace reserved for specific activities in which the operations of one or more airspace users is restricted. Also called ROZ.
terms.definition: 제한운항구역은 특정 활동에 예약된 항공 공간으로, 한 개 이상의 항공 공간 사용자의 운영이 제한됩니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.text: 제한운항구역에 진입하지 마세요. 위험할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Do not enter the restricted operations zone. It may be dangerous.

examples.text: 제한운항구역 경계에 주의하세요. 모든 비행은 안전하게 수행하세요.
examples.english: Be aware of the restricted operations zone boundaries. Conduct all flights safely.

terms.definitionEn: An area where flying drones is prohibited, usually around bases, airports and sensitive sites.
terms.definition: 무인기금지구역은 주로 기지와 공항, 민감한 시설 주변에서 드론 비행이 금지된 지역입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.english: Do not fly drones in the no-drone zone.

examples.text: 무인기금지구역 경계에 주의하세요. 모든 드론 작전을 안전하게 수행하세요.
examples.english: Be aware of the no-drone zone boundaries. Conduct all drone operations safely.

terms.definitionEn: A temporary ban or limit on flights in a defined area, announced to pilots, for example over an emergency or a VIP visit.
terms.definition: 비행이 금지되거나 제한되는 일시적인 조치로, 비상 상황이나 VIP 방문 시에 공지됩니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and briefings.

examples.text: 임시 비행 제한이 선언되었으므로, 해당 지역에 접근하지 마시오.
examples.english: A temporary flight restriction has been declared, so do not approach the area.

examples.text: 임시 비행 제한 구역은 오늘 오후까지 유효합니다.
examples.english: The temporary flight restriction area is valid until this afternoon.

terms.definitionEn: An air defense warning given in the form of a color code corresponding to the degree of air raid probability, with yellow standing for when an attack by hostile aircraft or missiles is probable, red for when an attack by hostile aircraft or missiles is imminent or is in progress, and white for when an attack by hostile aircraft or missiles is improbable. Also called ADWC.
terms.definition: 항공 방어 경보 상태는 적의 항공기나 미사일 공격 가능성에 따라 노란색(가능성 있음), 빨간색(즉시 또는 진행 중), 흰색(불가능)으로 구분되는 경보 체계입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and emergency broadcasts.

examples.text: 항공 방어 경보 상태가 노란색으로 상승했습니다.
examples.english: The air defense warning condition has risen to yellow.

examples.text: 항공 방어 경보 상태가 빨간색으로 변경되었으므로, 즉시 대피하시오.
examples.english: The air defense warning condition has changed to red, so evacuate immediately.

terms.definitionEn: A command and control facility established by the base commander to serve as the focal point for base security and defense. Also called BDOC.
terms.definition: 기지 방어 작전 센터는 기지 사령관이 설치한 명령 및 통제 시설로, 기지 보안과 방어의 중심점이 됩니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written reports and briefings.

examples.text: 기지 방어 작전 센터에서 긴급 회의가 열립니다.
examples.english: An emergency meeting is being held at the base defense operations center.

examples.text: 기지 방어 작전 센터는 모든 방어 활동을 조율합니다.
examples.english: The base defense operations center coordinates all defensive activities.

terms.definitionEn: The local military measures, both normal and emergency, required to nullify or reduce the effectiveness of enemy attacks on, or sabotage of, a base to ensure the maximum capacity of its facilities is available to United States forces.
terms.definition: 기지 방어는 적의 공격이나 테러로 인한 기지 시설의 손실을 최소화하기 위해 취하는 군사적 조치입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written reports and briefings.

examples.text: 기지방어를 강화하기 위해 추가 병력이 배치되었습니다.
examples.english: Additional troops have been deployed to bolster base defense.

examples.text: 기지방어는 모든 시설과 인력의 안전을 보장합니다.
examples.english: Base defense ensures the safety of all facilities and personnel.

terms.definitionEn: Preventive measures taken to mitigate hostile actions against Department of Defense personnel (including family members), resources, facilities, and critical information. Also called FP.
terms.definition: 력 보호는 국방부 인원, 자원, 시설, 중요 정보에 대한 적의 적대적 행위를 방지하기 위한 예방 조치입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written reports and briefings.

examples.text: 력 보호 조치를 강화하여 테러 위협에 대비하시오.
examples.english: Enhance force protection measures to counter terrorist threats.

examples.text: 력 보호는 모든 군사 활동의 기반입니다.
examples.english: Force protection is the foundation of all military operations.

terms.definitionEn: A Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff-approved standard for identification of and recommended responses to terrorist threats against United States personnel and facilities. Also called FPCON.
terms.definition: 력 보호 상태는 테러 위협에 대한 미국 인원과 시설의 대응을 위한 표준으로, 합동참모의장 승인을 받은 것입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and formal written reports.

examples.english: The force protection condition has risen to delta.

examples.text: 력 보호 상태가 브라보로 변경되었으므로, 경계를 강화하시오.
examples.english: The force protection condition has changed to bravo, so enhance vigilance.

terms.definitionEn: A guarded gate where people and vehicles are checked before they are allowed onto an installation.
terms.definition: 입장 통제 지점은 시설에 들어가는 사람과 차량을 검사하여 허용 여부를 결정하는 경비 게이트입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and signs.

examples.english: Present your ID at the entry control point.

examples.text: 입장 통제 지점은 기지 내 모든 교통의 진입점을 통제합니다.
examples.english: The entry control point controls all points of entry to the base.

terms.definitionEn: An area at or near an entry point, set apart from people and buildings, where vehicles are stopped and searched.
terms.definition: 차량 검색 구역은 인원과 건물에서 떨어진 진입점에서 차량을 정지하고 검색하는 공간입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and signs.

examples.text: 차량 검색 구역에 진입하기 전에 모든 문과 트렁크를 열으시오.
examples.english: Open all doors and trunks before entering the vehicle search area.

examples.text: 차량 검색 구역은 차량에 대한 철저한 검사를 수행합니다.
examples.english: The vehicle search area conducts thorough searches of vehicles.

terms.definitionEn: The outer boundary of a base or position, usually marked by fences or barriers and watched by guards.
terms.definition: 방어선은 기지나 위치를 둘러싸는 외곽 경계로, 주로 울타리나 장벽으로 표시되고 경비가 서 있습니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written reports and briefings.

examples.english: Mines have been laid to reinforce the perimeter.

examples.text: 방어선은 기지의 외곽을 보호하는 마지막 방어선입니다.
examples.english: The perimeter is the last line of defense protecting the base's outer boundary.

terms.definitionEn: An area of responsibility assigned to a unit; a sector sketch shows its boundaries, positions and fields of fire.
terms.definition: 구역은 부대에 할당된 책임 범위로, 경계, 위치, 사격 범위를 보여주는 구역 스케치에 표시됩니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and radio communications.

examples.english: Contact the unit responsible for the sector.

examples.text: 구역 경계에 대한 상세한 스케치는 보고서에 포함되어 있습니다.
examples.english: The detailed sector sketch is included in the report.

terms.definitionEn: A position from which soldiers watch an area and report what they see.
terms.definition: 군인이 특정 지역을 감시하고 보고하는 위치
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings to describe positions and their roles.

examples.english: The observation post is monitoring enemy movements.
The observation post has reported the enemy's location.

terms.definitionEn: A position placed in front of the defense, usually at night, to give early warning by listening for enemy movement.
terms.definition: 방어선 앞, 주로 밤에 적의 움직임을 듣고 조기에 경고하는 위치
terms.registerNote: Typically used in radio communications and reports for early warning.

examples.english: The listening post has detected enemy approach.
Suspicious noises have been picked up at the listening post.

terms.definitionEn: A unit kept ready to move at short notice to respond to an incident or reinforce a threatened area.
terms.definition: 사고에 대응하거나 위협받는 지역에 증원하기 위해 즉시 이동할 수 있도록 준비된 부대
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and radio communications to discuss force readiness.

examples.text: 신속 대응 부대가 출동 준비가 완료되었습니다.
examples.english: The quick reaction force is ready to deploy.
The quick reaction force has arrived at the scene.

terms.definitionEn: Duly constituted military, paramilitary, police, and constabulary forces of a state.
terms.definition: 국가의 정식 군사, 준군사, 경찰, 헌병 등 모든 보안 부대
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings to describe security measures.

examples.english: Security forces are patrolling the base.
Security forces have apprehended an intruder.

terms.definitionEn: A member of a security force on duty protecting a base, its people and its resources.
terms.definition: 기지의 사람들과 자산을 보호하는 임무를 수행하는 보안 요원
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings to describe the role of security personnel.

examples.english: The defender maintains the base's security.
The defender has discovered suspicious activity.

terms.definitionEn: A detachment sent out to gather information or provide security, on foot (dismounted) or in vehicles (mounted).
terms.definition: 보행 또는 차량을 이용해 정보를 수집하거나 보안을 제공하기 위해 파견된 소대
terms.registerNote: Used in reports, radio communications, and briefings to discuss security measures.

examples.english: Found enemy traces during patrol.
We need to reinforce patrol activities.

terms.definitionEn: A security measure applied at irregular times and places so that an attacker cannot predict the defense.
terms.definition: 공격자가 방어의 패턴을 예측할 수 없도록 불규칙한 시간과 장소에 적용되는 보안 조치
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings to describe security measures.

examples.english: Set up a checkpoint as a random antiterrorism measure.

examples.text: 무작위 대테러 조치로 차량 검사를 실시합니다.
examples.english: Conducting vehicle checks as a random antiterrorism measure.

terms.definitionEn: The distance kept between a possible bomb, such as a vehicle, and the people or buildings it could harm.
terms.definition: 폭탄이 될 수 있는 차량과 그 피해를 입을 수 있는 사람이나 건물 사이의 거리
terms.registerNote: Used in safety briefings and reports.

examples.english: The standoff distance must be maintained at 500 meters or more.

examples.text: 안전 거리가 부족할 경우, 폭발 위험이 있습니다.
examples.english: If the standoff distance is insufficient, there is a risk of explosion.

terms.definitionEn: Any obstruction or coordinated series of obstacles designed or employed to channel, direct, restrict, delay, or stop movement.
terms.definition: 이동을 유도, 제한, 지연, 또는 중단하기 위해 설치된 장애물 또는 장애물들의 조합
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports, formal register.

examples.english: The barriers are slowing down the enemy's advance.
The barrier removal task has been completed.

terms.definitionEn: Measures, such as barriers, film on windows and distance, that reduce the harm an explosion can do.
terms.definition: 폭발의 피해를 줄이기 위해 설치하는 장벽, 창문에 붙이는 필름, 거리 등 조치
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings to describe safety measures.

examples.english: Installed blast mitigation devices.
Reduced damage through blast mitigation measures.

terms.definitionEn: A posted state that tells everyone on a base whether an attack is unlikely, expected or under way, and what protective action to take.
terms.definition: 기지가 공격받을 위험이 있는지, 공격이 예상되는지, 또는 공격이 진행 중인지 알려주는 상태를 나타내는 것. 이 상태는 보호 조치를 취할 것을 알려줌.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and radio communications.

examples.text: 경보 상태가 변경되었습니다. 모든 인원은 즉시 대피하세요.
examples.english: The alarm condition has changed. Everyone must evacuate immediately.

examples.text: 경보 상태는 현재 DEFCON 2입니다. 모든 인원은 전투 준비 상태를 유지하세요.
examples.english: The current alarm condition is DEFCON 2. All personnel must maintain battle readiness.

terms.definitionEn: The check of a base after an attack to find damage, casualties and unexploded ordnance.
terms.definition: 기지가 공격받은 후 피해, 사상자, 그리고 미폭발 폭탄을 확인하는 활동.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and radio communications.

examples.text: 사후 정찰 팀은 즉시 피해 지역으로 이동하세요.
examples.english: The post-attack reconnaissance team must move to the affected area immediately.

examples.text: 사후 정찰 보고서에 따르면, 피해는 최소한으로 끝났습니다.
examples.english: According to the post-attack reconnaissance report, damage was minimal.

terms.definitionEn: Explosive ordnance that has been primed, fused, armed, or otherwise prepared for action and has been fired, dropped, launched, projected, or placed in such a manner as to constitute a hazard to operations, installations, personnel, or material and remains unexploded either by malfunction or design or for any other cause. Also called UXO.
terms.definition: 폭발물이나 폭탄이 작동하지 않고 남아 있어 위험한 상태를 말함.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and radio communications.

examples.text: 미폭발 폭탄이 발견되었습니다. 즉시 해당 지역을 봉쇄하세요.
examples.english: An unexploded explosive ordnance has been found. Seal off the area immediately.

examples.text: 미폭발 폭탄 처리반은 즉시 현장으로 출동하세요.
examples.english: The unexploded ordnance disposal team must deploy to the scene immediately.

terms.definitionEn: To stay indoors or in the nearest protected place until told it is safe to move.
terms.definition: 안전한 장소에 머무르거나 가장 가까운 보호 장소로 이동하여 위험이 지나갈 때까지 기다리는 것.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and announcements.

examples.english: Shelter in place. Going outside is prohibited.

examples.text: 현장에서 대기 중인 모든 인원은 재량 이동을 금지합니다.
examples.english: All personnel sheltering in place must not move without permission.

terms.definitionEn: A reinforced shelter, often of concrete or sandbags, that protects people from blast and fragments.
terms.definition: 폭발이나 파편으로부터 사람들을 보호하기 위해 강화된 콘크리트나 모래주머니로 만든 쉼터.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and orders, urgent situations.

examples.english: Take cover in the bunker!
The bunker protected our troops from the airstrike.

terms.definitionEn: Cover protects from fire; concealment only hides from view.
terms.definition: 보호는 화로부터 보호하는 것이지만, 은폐는 단순히 시야에서 숨기는 것.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and training.

examples.text: 보호와 은폐를 확보하세요. 모든 인원은 즉시 행동하세요.
examples.english: Secure cover and concealment. All personnel must act immediately.

examples.text: 보호와 은폐를 확보할 수 있는 위치로 이동하세요.
examples.english: Move to a position where you can secure cover and concealment.

terms.definitionEn: Knowing where every person is and whether they are safe, especially after an attack or alarm.
terms.definition: 특히 공격이나 경보 후 모든 사람이 안전하고 어디에 있는지를 확인하는 것.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and radio communications.

examples.text: 인원 확인을 완료하세요. 모든 인원의 안전 상태를 보고하세요.
examples.english: Complete accountability. Report the safety status of all personnel.

examples.text: 인원 확인 결과, 모든 인원이 안전합니다.
examples.english: Accountability results: All personnel are safe.

terms.definitionEn: An order that stops all movement on an installation or in a building until the threat has passed.
terms.definition: 기지나 건물 내에서 위협이 지나갈 때까지 모든 이동을 중단하는 명령.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and announcements.

examples.text: 봉쇄령이 내려졌습니다. 모든 인원은 즉시 현 위치에서 대기하세요.
examples.english: Lockdown has been ordered. All personnel must wait at their current location immediately.

examples.text: 봉쇄령이 해제될 때까지 모든 인원은 해당 건물에서 대기하세요.
examples.english: All personnel must wait in their respective buildings until lockdown is lifted.

terms.definitionEn: The announcement that a threat has ended and normal activity may resume.
terms.definition: 위협이 끝났고 정상적인 활동이 재개될 수 있음을 알리는 선언.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and announcements.

examples.text: 전원 안전입니다. 모든 인원은 정상 업무로 복귀하세요.
examples.english: All clear. All personnel may return to normal duties.

examples.text: 전원 안전 신호가 울렸습니다. 모든 인원은 즉시 복귀하세요.
examples.english: The all-clear signal has sounded. All personnel must return immediately.

terms.definitionEn: The person in charge of all response activity at the scene of an incident.
terms.definition: 사고 현장에서 모든 응답 활동을 책임지는 사람.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and radio communications.

examples.english: The incident commander must move to the scene immediately.

examples.text: 현장 책임자는 모든 응답 활동을 조정합니다.
examples.english: The incident commander coordinates all response activities.

terms.definitionEn: A headquarters for the coordination of information and resources to support incident management activities. Also called EOC.
terms.definition: 비상작전센터는 재난 관리 활동을 지원하기 위해 정보를 조정하고 자원을 지원하는 본부입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.english: The emergency operations center coordinates all emergency situations.

examples.text: 모든 부대는 비상작전센터와 지속적으로 연락 유지해야 합니다.
examples.english: All units must maintain constant contact with the emergency operations center.

terms.definitionEn: A system that warns everyone on an installation at once, through sirens, loudspeakers, phones and computers.
terms.definition: 대량통지시스템은 시레, 스피커, 전화, 컴퓨터 등을 통해 시설 내 모든 사람에게 동시에 경고를 발송하는 시스템입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used for radio and written reports.

examples.text: 대량통지시스템을 통해 모든 인원에게 경보를 발령했다.
examples.english: We issued a warning to all personnel through the mass notification system.
The mass notification system activated, sending an emergency message.

terms.definitionEn: Fire, such as mortar, rocket or artillery rounds, aimed at a target the firer cannot see, usually along a high curved path.
terms.definition: 간접사격은 포병, 로켓 또는 박격포와 같은 무기로, 사수가 목표물을 직접 볼 수 없는 상태에서 곡선을 그리며 발사하는 것입니다.
terms.registerNote: Common in reports and briefings.

examples.text: 적의 간접사격으로 인해 전방 부대가 피해를 입었습니다.
examples.english: Our forward units suffered damage from enemy indirect fire.
The artillery unit attacked the target with indirect fire.

terms.definitionEn: C-RAM is a tactical mission that provides detection, warning, C2, and intercept of RAM in flight and engagement of enemy sources of IDF.
terms.definition: 대포병 레이더는 적의 포병 사격과 간접 화력을 탐지하고 경고하며, 적의 포병을 공격하는 임무를 수행합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: The counter-rocket, artillery, and mortar radar detected enemy fire.

examples.text: 대포병 레이더의 경고로 인해 부대는 신속하게 대응했습니다.
examples.english: The unit responded quickly to the counter-rocket, artillery, and mortar radar warning.

terms.definitionEn: The risk that a person with authorized access, such as an employee or contractor, uses that access to cause harm.
terms.definition: 내부위협은 직원이나 계약자와 같은 권한이 있는 사람이 그 권한을 악용하여 피해를 입힐 수 있는 위험을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and written guidance.

examples.text: 내부위협으로 인해 기밀 정보가 유출될 위험이 있습니다.
examples.english: There is a risk of classified information leaking due to insider threat.

examples.text: 모든 직원은 내부위협에 대한 교육을 받아야 합니다.
examples.english: All personnel must receive training on insider threat.

terms.definitionEn: A nation that allows forces to operate in or to transit through its territory. Also called HN.
terms.definition: 주요국은 군대가 작전을 수행하거나 통과할 수 있도록 영토를 제공하는 국가를 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings.

examples.english: We conducted the operation in cooperation with the host nation.

examples.text: 주요국의 지원으로 인해 작전이 성공적으로 완료되었습니다.
examples.english: The operation was successfully completed with the support of the host nation.

terms.definitionEn: Personnel organized and/or employed for security, whether they are civil or military, federal, state or provincial, or local. Also called FSF.
terms.definition: 외국안보군은 보안 임무를 수행하는 민간 또는 군인, 연방, 주 또는 지방 정부 소속의 인원을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and liaison communications.

examples.english: Foreign security forces assist with local security.
We conducted training in cooperation with foreign security forces.

terms.definitionEn: A bilateral or multilateral agreement that defines the legal position of a visiting military force deployed in the territory of a friendly state. Also called SOFA.
terms.definition: SOFA는 친선국 영토에 주둔하는 군사 부대의 법적 지위를 정의하는 양자 또는 다자간 협정입니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written communication and briefings.

examples.text: 주둔군지위협정(SOFA)에 따라 우리 군은 해당 국가의 법률을 준수해야 합니다.
examples.english: According to the SOFA, our military must comply with the host nation's laws.
We will begin renegotiating the SOFA.

terms.definitionEn: The legal authority to investigate, arrest and try people for offenses in a given place.
terms.definition: 관할권은 특정 지역에서 범죄를 조사, 체포 및 재판할 수 있는 법적 권한을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio and written reports.

examples.english: This incident is not within our jurisdiction.
We reported the incident to the jurisdiction police station.

terms.definitionEn: A citizen of the host country, for example one working on or near a base.
terms.definition: 현지인은 예를 들어 기지 근처에서 일하는 숙국 시민을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and liaison communications.

examples.text: 현지인은 기지에 출입할 때 신분증을 제시해야 합니다.
examples.english: Local nationals must present identification when entering the base.

examples.text: 현지인과 협력하여 지역 사회와의 관계를 개선했습니다.
examples.english: We improved relations with the local community by cooperating with local nationals.

terms.definitionEn: A person assigned to accompany a visitor or contractor who may not move on the base alone.
terms.definition: 방문객이나 계약자에게 동행하여 혼자서 기지 내에서 이동하지 않도록 하는 임무에 배치된 사람
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports, formal.

examples.text: 호위병이 방문자를 동행하여 건물 내로 안내했습니다.
examples.english: The escort accompanied the visitor and guided them into the building.

examples.text: 호위병이 계약자에게 기지 내 이동을 지원하고 있습니다.
examples.english: The escort is assisting the contractor with movement within the base.

terms.definitionEn: The list of people authorized to enter a facility or area, checked against their badges.
terms.definition: 시설이나 구역에 출입할 수 있는 인원 목록으로, 출입 시 신분증을 확인하는 용도로 사용됩니다
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and at checkpoints, formal.

examples.text: 출입명단에 없는 사람은 시설에 출입할 수 없습니다.
examples.english: Persons not on the access roster may not enter the facility.
The guard checked the access roster and permitted entry.

terms.definitionEn: Passing the current situation, open issues and equipment from one duty shift to the next.
terms.definition: 당직 교대 시 현재 상황, 미해결 문제, 장비 상태 등을 다음 당직자에게 전달하는 과정
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and during shift changes, formal.

examples.text: 교대인계 시 현재 상황을 상세히 설명해야 합니다.
examples.english: During shift handover, you must describe the current situation in detail.

examples.text: 교대인계 과정에서 발생한 문제를 다음 교대조에 전달했습니다.
examples.english: We conveyed the issues that arose during shift handover to the next shift.

terms.definitionEn: The chronological log in which a security or police desk records incidents and actions.
terms.definition: 보안 또는 경찰 당직자가 발생한 사건과 조치를 시간 순으로 기록하는 로그
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and during shift changes, formal.

examples.text: 경비일지에 사건 발생 시점을 정확히 기록해야 합니다.
examples.english: The blotter must accurately record the time of incident occurrence.

examples.text: 경비일지를 통해 어제 발생한 사건을 확인했습니다.
examples.english: We checked yesterday's incidents through the blotter.

terms.definitionEn: The written record of everyone who has held a piece of evidence, from collection onward, so it can be trusted.
terms.definition: 증거를 수집한 이후부터 보관한 모든 사람의 기록을 작성하여 증거의 신뢰성을 보장하는 과정
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and investigations, formal.

examples.text: 증거보관연계를 통해 증거의 무결성을 유지해야 합니다.
examples.english: The chain of custody must maintain the integrity of the evidence.

examples.text: 증거보관연계 기록을 통해 증거의 이동 경로를 추적했습니다.
examples.english: We traced the movement of the evidence through the chain of custody records.

terms.definitionEn: The exercise of delegated authority over designated airspace and users through control procedures and coordination measures to maximize operational effectiveness.
terms.definition: 특정 공역과 사용자에 대한 권한을 위임받아 통제 절차와 조정 조치를 통해 작전 효율성을 극대화하는 행위
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and radio communications, formal.

examples.text: 공역통제를 통해 항공기들의 안전한 운항을 보장합니다.
examples.english: Airspace control ensures the safe operation of aircraft.

examples.text: 공역통제 권한을 부여받아 해당 공역에서 항공임을 수행했습니다.
examples.english: We performed air missions in the designated airspace after being granted airspace control authority.

terms.definitionEn: A method used to task and disseminate to components, subordinate units, and command and control agencies projected sorties, capabilities, or forces for targeting and specific missions. Also called ATO.
terms.definition: 부대, 하위 부대, 지휘 통제 기관에 정찰 임무, 능력, 또는 타겟팅 및 특정 임무를 위한 병력을 할당하고 배포하는 방법
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and planning, formal.

examples.text: 항공임무지시서는 매일 발행되어 각 부대에 배포됩니다.
examples.english: The air tasking order is issued daily and distributed to each unit.
We will carry out today's missions according to the air tasking order.

terms.definitionEn: Weapons and equipment for actively combating air targets from the ground. Also called ADA.
terms.definition: 지상에서 공중 표적을 적극적으로 공격하는 무기 및 장비
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and training, formal.

examples.text: 방공포병은 항공기로부터 기지를 방어하는 역할을 합니다.
examples.english: Air defense artillery protects the base from aircraft.
The air defense artillery detected and shot down the enemy aircraft.

terms.definitionEn: A device that emits a signal positively identifying it as a friendly. Also called IFF.
terms.definition: 신호로 발신하여 친절한 신원을 긍정적으로 식별하는 장치
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings, reports, and radio communications, formal.

examples.text: 적아식별장치는 우리 항공기를 적으로부터 구분하는 데 사용됩니다.
examples.english: The IFF device is used to distinguish our aircraft from the enemy.
We activated the IFF device and were identified as a friendly aircraft.

terms.definitionEn: The code an aircraft's transponder sends; 'squawk' is also the order to set that code.
terms.definition: 항공기의 트랜스폰더가 보내는 코드; '스콰크'는 그 코드를 설정하라는 명령이기도 합니다
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports, formal.

examples.text: 항공기는 스콰크 코드를 설정하여 정체성을 확인합니다.
examples.english: Aircraft set their squawk code to confirm their identity.
We set squawk 7500 to signal an emergency.

terms.definitionEn: A band of altitudes, between a lower and an upper limit, assigned to one aircraft or activity.
terms.definition: 고도대는 항공기나 활동에 할당된, 아래와 위 한계가 있는 고도대이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio and written reports for altitude management.

examples.english: "Unit 123, maintain altitude block from 18,000 to 22,000 feet."
"The altitude block is engaged between 12,000 and 16,000 feet."

terms.definitionEn: Coordinating times, places and altitudes so that friendly aircraft, drones and fires do not interfere with or endanger each other.
terms.definition: 충돌회피는 항공기, 드론, 화력이 서로 간섭하거나 위험에 처하지 않도록 시간, 장소, 고도를 조정하는 것이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and briefings for coordination.

examples.text: 모든 항공기, 충돌회피를 위해 10마일 간격을 유지하시오.
examples.english: "All aircraft, maintain 10-mile separation for deconfliction."
"Confirm deconfliction between drones and aircraft."

terms.definitionEn: A three-dimensional permissive fire support coordination measure with an associated airspace coordinating measure used to facilitate the integration of fires.
terms.definition: 킬박스는 화력 통합을 용이하게 하기 위해 사용되는 3차원적 화력 지원 조율 측정과 관련된 공역 조율 측정이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in fire support coordination and planning.

examples.english: "Requesting fire support for kill box 5-A."
"The kill box is set to a 10km x 10km area."

terms.definitionEn: Any combination of characters or pronounceable words, which identifies a communication facility, a command, an authority, an activity, or a unit; used primarily for establishing and maintaining communications. Also called CS.
terms.definition: 호출부호는 통신 설정을 위해 사용되는 문자 또는 발음 가능한 단어의 조합으로, 시설, 명령, 권한, 활동 또는 단위를 식별한다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and liaison.

examples.english: The call sign is "Red 1".
Please connect using the call sign.

terms.definitionEn: A code word, which provides no security, that serves the sole purpose of shortening of messages rather than the concealment of their content.
terms.definition: 간결어는 메시지를 단축하기 위한 암호 단어로, 보안보다는 내용의 숨김에 중점을 두지 않는다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to shorten messages.

examples.english: "Use brevity code 'EMCON' to report current status."
"Use brevity code 'BREAK BREAK' to announce an emergency."

terms.definitionEn: The radio call in which a unit or aircraft reports to a controller that it has arrived and is ready, with its status.
terms.definition: 체크인은 단위가 도착하여 준비가 되었고 상태를 보고하는 무전 호출이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication for arrival reporting.

examples.english: "Unit 123, check-in."

examples.text: 체크인 후, 임무 준비 완료를 보고하시오.
examples.english: "After check-in, report mission readiness."

terms.definitionEn: A report giving the situation in the area of a reporting unit or formation. Also called SITREP.
terms.definition: 상황보고는 보고 단위 또는 형성의 영역에서 상황을 설명하는 보고서이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in written reports and briefings for situational awareness.

examples.english: "Requesting current situation report."
"According to the situation report, enemy movement has been confirmed."

terms.definitionEn: A concise narrative report of essential information covering events or conditions that may have an immediate and significant effect on current planning and operations that is afforded the most expeditious means of transmission consistent with requisite security. Also called SPOTREP. (Note: In reconnaissance and surveillance usage, spot report is not to be used.)
terms.definition: 즉각보고는 현재 계획 및 작전에 즉각적이고 중요한 영향을 미칠 수 있는 사건이나 상태를 간결하게 설명하는 보고서로, 가능한 한 신속한 전송이 이루어져야 한다.
terms.registerNote: Used in urgent situations to report significant events.

examples.english: "Spot report: Enemy artillery fire has begun."
"Spot reports must be relayed to higher headquarters immediately."

terms.definitionEn: The standard nine-line radio message used to request evacuation of casualties, giving location, frequency, number of patients and other essentials.
terms.definition: 의료후송요청은 환자의 위치, 주파수, 환자 수 등을 포함한 필수 정보를 제공하는 표준 9라인 무전 메시지로, 환자 후송을 요청하는 데 사용된다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication for medical evacuation requests.

examples.text: 의료후송요청을 시작하시오: 첫 번째 줄은 현재 위치입니다.
examples.english: "Initiate nine-line medical evacuation request: First line is current location."

examples.text: 의료후송요청의 여덟 번째 줄은 환자의 상태입니다.
examples.english: "The eighth line of the nine-line medical evacuation request is the patient's condition."

terms.definitionEn: A map position given as letters and numbers of a grid system such as MGRS.
terms.definition: 좌표는 MGRS와 같은 그리드 시스템의 글자와 숫자로 주어진 지도의 위치이다.
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication and written reports for location reference.

examples.english: "Current grid reference is 42S QA 123456."

examples.text: 좌표를 확인 후, 다음 목표로 이동하시오.
examples.english: "Confirm grid reference and proceed to the next target."

terms.definitionEn: The direction to an object measured clockwise from north, in degrees.
terms.definition: 물체의 방향을 북쪽을 기준으로 시계 방향으로 측정하여 각도로 나타낸 것
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports for precise navigation.

examples.english: The bearing is 090 degrees.
The target's bearing is 270 degrees.

terms.definitionEn: The actual time at which munitions impact the target. Also called TOT.
terms.definition: 무기가 목표물에 명중하는 실제 시간
terms.registerNote: Used in planning and coordination for munitions delivery.

examples.english: Time on target is 1430 hours.
Time on target has been adjusted to 1515 hours.

terms.definitionEn: A CONTACT whose identity is unknown.
terms.definition: 신원이 알려지지 않은 접촉 대상
terms.registerNote: Used to report unidentified contacts in radio communications.

examples.english: A bogey has been picked up on radar.
The bogey is changing direction.

terms.definitionEn: 1. [A/A] [AIR-MAR] Positively identified as an enemy in accordance with (IAW) theater ID criteria. The term does not imply direction or authority to engage. 2. * [SO] A SUSPECT whose orbital parameters are such that it may become a collection and/or counterspace concern to a spacecraft in the relative near-term, therefore limiting decision space.
terms.definition: 적으로 확인된 접촉 대상
terms.registerNote: Used to report positively identified enemy contacts in radio communications.

examples.english: Bandits are approaching.
Bandits are at 2 o'clock.

terms.definitionEn: A contact identified as enemy upon which clearance to fire is authorized IAW theater rules of engagement (ROE). WARNING This use of HOSTILE is as a brevity term for air engagements and should not be confused with the same term in tactical data link identification.
terms.definition: 화력 사용이 허용된 적대적인 접촉 대상
terms.registerNote: Used to report enemy contacts authorized to engage in radio communications.

examples.english: Hostile confirmed.
The hostile is exposed to firepower.

terms.definitionEn: A positively identified FRIENDLY aircraft, ship, spacecraft, or ground position.
terms.definition: 확인된 우호적인 항공기, 선박, 우주선 또는 지상 위치
terms.registerNote: Used to report friendly forces in radio communications and briefings.

examples.english: Friendlies are at 12 o'clock.
We will perform the mission in cooperation with friendlies.

terms.definitionEn: 1. A code meaning “information not available.” 2. An aircraft or ship that has not been determined to be hostile, friendly, or neutral. 3. An identity applied to an evaluated track that has not been identified.
terms.definition: 적대적이거나 우호적이거나 중립적인 것으로 확인되지 않은 항공기 또는 선박
terms.registerNote: Used to report unidentified contacts in radio communications and briefings.

examples.english: An unknown aircraft is approaching.
The unknown's identity has been confirmed.

terms.definitionEn: 1. [A/A] [A/S] [S/A] Hit observed with valid DWE against a target. 2. * [S/A] [S/S] Informative call to observer or spotter 5 seconds prior to estimated time of impact.
terms.definition: 목표물에 대한 유효한 DWE와 함께 관측된 명중
terms.registerNote: Used to report hits on targets in radio communications.

examples.english: Splash confirmed.
Splash in 5 seconds.

terms.definitionEn: Radar warning receiver indication of an air interceptor threat in track or launch.
terms.definition: 레이더 경보 수신기에서 추적 또는 발사된 공중 요격 위협을 나타내는 표시
terms.registerNote: Used to report radar threats in radio communications.

examples.english: Spike detected.
The spike is approaching us.

terms.definitionEn: 1.* [A/A] [A/S] [S/A] [SO] Aircrew does not have visual contact with the TARGET or BANDIT. Opposite of TALLY. 2.* Indicates that radio communications could not be established with the distant end on a specified radio net.
terms.definition: 조종사가 목표물이나 적대 항공기를 시각적으로 확인하지 못하는 상태
terms.registerNote: Used to report lack of visual contact in radio communications.

examples.english: No joy.
No joy, visibility is obscured.

terms.definitionEn: Sighting of a target, non-friendly aircraft, or enemy position. Opposite of NO JOY.
terms.definition: 적기나 적의 위치를 발견한 것을 말합니다. "NO JOY"의 반대입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to report sightings.

examples.english: Enemy aircraft is TALLY.
Confirmed TALLY on radar target.

terms.definitionEn: Prebriefed fuel state needed for recovery.
terms.definition: 항공기가 안전하게 귀환하기 위해 필요한 연료 상태를 말합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in prebriefs and fuel status reports.

examples.english: Current fuel state is BINGO.
Reached BINGO state.

terms.definitionEn: Stop firing, do not open fire. Missiles in flight will continue to intercept; continue to track.
terms.definition: 사격을 중단하고 발사하지 말라는 명령입니다. 이미 발사된 미사일은 계속 목표물을 추적합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in orders and reports to stop firing.

examples.english: All units, CEASE FIRE.
Confirmed CEASE FIRE order.

terms.definitionEn: Weapons control status. Fire only: 1. * FREE: at targets not identified as FRIENDLY IAW current ROE. 2. * TIGHT: at targets positively identified as HOSTILE IAW current ROE. 3. * HOLD/SAFE: in self-defense or in response to a formal order. NOTE NATO uses WEAPONS to determine munitions available or remaining, similar to WHAT STATE.
terms.definition: 무기의 사용 상태를 말합니다. FREE는 현재 ROE에 따라 FRIENDLY로 식별되지 않은 목표물에 대한 사격을 허용하고, TIGHT는 HOSTILE로 확인된 목표물에 대한 사격을 허용하며, HOLD/SAFE는 자위나 공식 명령에 따라 사격을 중지합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in weapons control status reports.

examples.english: Current WEAPONS status is TIGHT.
Execute WEAPONS FREE.

terms.definitionEn: Radio procedure word: wait, I will answer shortly.
terms.definition: 라디오 통신에서 "잠시 기다리세요, 곧 답변하겠습니다"라는 의미입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to indicate waiting.

examples.english: Please STAND BY.
Standing by.

terms.definitionEn: Radio procedure word: repeat your last message, or the part named.
terms.definition: 라디오 통신에서 "마지막 메시지를 다시 반복해 주세요"라는 의미입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to request repetition.

examples.english: SAY AGAIN your last message.
SAY AGAIN the code part.

terms.definitionEn: Radio transmission received; does not indicate compliance or reaction.
terms.definition: 라디오 메시지가 수신되었음을 나타내지만, 준수나 반응을 의미하지는 않습니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to acknowledge receipt.

examples.english: Message received, ROGER.
Confirmed, ROGER.

terms.definitionEn: Will comply with received instructions.
terms.definition: 수신한 지시에 따라 행동할 것을 의미합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to indicate compliance.

examples.english: Command received, WILCO.
Will comply, WILCO.

terms.definitionEn: Radio procedure words that interrupt traffic on a busy net to pass an urgent message.
terms.definition: 바쁜 네트워크에서 긴급한 메시지를 전달하기 위해 통신을 중단하는 라디오 절차 단어입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communication to interrupt traffic.

examples.english: Urgent message, BREAK BREAK.
Important info, BREAK BREAK.

terms.definitionEn: The right to give orders and make decisions within a defined area of responsibility.
terms.definition: 특정 책임 범위 내에서 명령하고 결정을 내릴 권리를 말합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in formal written reports and briefings.

examples.english: I have the authority for this task.
Actions without authority are prohibited.

terms.definitionEn: The action by which a commander assigns part of his or her authority, commensurate with the assigned task, to a subordinate commander.
terms.definition: 상급자가 부하 장교에게 권한을 일정 부분 위임하는 것, 주어진 임무에 맞게
terms.registerNote: Formal, written, command-level.

examples.text: 권한 위임은 작전 계획에 따라 하급 부대에 이행되어야 합니다.
examples.english: Delegation of authority should be carried out to subordinate units according to the operation plan.

examples.text: 이 작전에서 권한 위임은 매우 중요합니다.
examples.english: Delegation of authority is very important in this operation.

terms.definitionEn: A commander or individual who has the authority to require consultation between the specific functions or activities involving forces of two or more Services, joint force components, or forces of the same Service or agencies but does not have the authority to compel agreement.
terms.definition: 여러 부대의 조율을 요구할 수 있지만 합의를 강제할 수 없는 권한을 가진 장교나 개인을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Formal, command-level, written or radio.

examples.text: 조정 권한은 다중 부대 간 협력을 보장합니다.
examples.english: Coordinating authority ensures cooperation among multiple units.

examples.text: 조정 권한을 가진 사령관은 모든 관련 부대와 협의해야 합니다.
examples.english: The commander with coordinating authority must consult with all relevant units.

terms.definitionEn: Formal agreement by the person with authority that an action may go ahead.
terms.definition: 권한 있는 사람이 어떤 행동을 진행할 수 있도록 공식적으로 동의하는 것
terms.registerNote: Formal, written, command-level.

examples.text: 승인은 작전 실행 전에 반드시 필요합니다.
examples.english: Approval is absolutely necessary before executing an operation.

examples.text: 이 계획은 상급자의 승인을 받아야 합니다.
examples.english: This plan needs to be approved by a superior.

terms.definitionEn: Contact kept between units or organizations so that they understand each other and act together.
terms.definition: 부대나 조직 간 서로 이해하고 협력할 수 있도록 연락하는 것
terms.registerNote: Formal, radio or written, liaison officers.

examples.english: Liaison is essential for operational success.

examples.text: 연락 장교는 부대 간 협조를 촉진합니다.
examples.english: The liaison officer promotes cooperation between units.

terms.definitionEn: The ability to act together coherently, effectively, and efficiently to achieve tactical, operational, and strategic objectives.
terms.definition: 전술, 작전, 전략 목표를 달성하기 위해 협력적으로, 효과적으로, 효율적으로 행동할 수 있는 능력
terms.registerNote: Formal, written or radio, multinational contexts.

examples.english: Interoperability is important in multinational operations.

examples.text: 상호운용성을 높이기 위해 표준화된 절차를 사용해야 합니다.
examples.english: To enhance interoperability, we must use standardized procedures.

terms.definitionEn: Giving partners the information they need, within the limits of its classification and release rules.
terms.definition: 파트너에게 필요한 정보를 분류 수준과 공개 규칙 내에서 제공하는 것
terms.registerNote: Formal, written or radio, sensitive contexts.

examples.english: Information sharing ensures operational success.

examples.text: 정보 공유를 위해 안전한 채널을 사용해야 합니다.
examples.english: To share information, we must use secure channels.

terms.definitionEn: A restriction a nation places on how its forces may be used, or on who may see a piece of information.
terms.definition: 국가가 자신의 부대 사용에 대한 제한이나 정보 공개에 대한 제한을 의미합니다.
terms.registerNote: Formal, written, command-level.

examples.text: 제약조건은 작전의 범위를 제한할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Caveats can limit the scope of an operation.

examples.text: 이 작전에 대한 제약조건을 명확히 해야 합니다.
examples.english: We must clearly define the caveats for this operation.

terms.definitionEn: The determination that official information requires, in the interests of national security, a specific degree of protection against unauthorized disclosure, coupled with a designation signifying that such a determination has been made.
terms.definition: 국가 안보를 위해 정보가 특정 보호 수준이 필요함을 결정하고, 그 결정이 내려졌음을 표시하는 표시를 부여하는 것
terms.registerNote: Formal, written, security contexts.

examples.text: 분류는 정보의 보안을 유지하는 데 중요합니다.
examples.english: Classification is important for maintaining information security.

examples.text: 이 문서는 비밀 분류로 처리되어야 합니다.
examples.english: This document must be treated as classified.

terms.definitionEn: Formal permission to give classified or controlled information to a partner nation or organization.
terms.definition: 기밀이나 통제된 정보를 파트너 국가나 조직에 공개할 수 있는 공식적인 허가
terms.registerNote: Formal, written, security contexts.

examples.english: Information release must be done carefully.

examples.text: 정보 공개 전에 모든 관련 부서와 협의해야 합니다.
examples.english: Before releasing information, we must consult all relevant departments.

terms.definitionEn: A military maneuver or simulated wartime operation involving planning, preparation, and execution that is carried out for the purpose of training and evaluation.
terms.definition: 계획, 준비, 실행 과정을 통해 훈련과 평가를 목적으로 하는 군사적 기동 또는 가상 전쟁 작전을 수행하는 것
terms.registerNote: Formal, written or radio, training contexts.

examples.english: Exercises are essential for real operations.
This exercise includes multinational units.

terms.definitionEn: A short, repeated practice of a set procedure so that it becomes automatic.
terms.definition: 훈련은 특정 절차를 반복적으로 연습하여 자동적으로 수행할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and instructions.

examples.text: 훈련을 시작하기 전에 모든 장비를 점검하십시오.
examples.english: Check all equipment before starting the drill.

examples.text: 이 훈련은 전투 상황에서의 대응력을 향상시키기 위해 설계되었습니다.
examples.english: This drill is designed to improve response capabilities in combat situations.

terms.definitionEn: The imagined situation and events on which an exercise is built.
terms.definition: 시나리오는 연습이나 훈련을 위해 가정되는 상황과 사건입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in planning and briefings.

examples.text: 이번 연습의 시나리오는 적의 기습 공격에 대한 대응입니다.
examples.english: The scenario for this exercise is responding to an enemy's surprise attack.

examples.text: 시나리오에 따라 모든 부대는 즉시 대응해야 합니다.
examples.english: According to the scenario, all units must respond immediately.

terms.definitionEn: Lessons learned are validated knowledge and experience derived from observations and the historical study of military training, exercises, and combat operations that lead to a change in behavior.
terms.definition: 교훈은 군사 훈련, 연습, 전투 작전을 통해 얻은 검증된 지식과 경험으로, 행동 변화를 이끌어냅니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and debriefings.

examples.text: 이번 작전에서 얻은 교훈은 향후 작전에 반영되어야 합니다.
examples.english: The lessons learned from this operation should be incorporated into future operations.

examples.text: 교훈을 통해 우리는 우리의 약점을 파악할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Through lessons learned, we can identify our weaknesses.

terms.definitionEn: A structured discussion after an event or exercise about what was supposed to happen, what happened, why, and what to do differently.
terms.definition: 사후 검토는 어떤 일이 일어났는지, 왜 일어났는지, 그리고 다음에 어떻게 다르게 해야 하는지 논의하는 구조화된 회의입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in debriefings and reports.

examples.text: 사후 검토를 통해 우리는 어떤 부분이 개선이 필요했는지 확인할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: Through the after-action review, we can identify areas that need improvement.

examples.text: 사후 검토 회의는 내일 오전 9시에 개최됩니다.
examples.english: The after-action review meeting will be held tomorrow at 9 AM.

terms.definitionEn: The commander designated for overall responsibility for airspace control. Also called ACA.
terms.definition: 항공통제권자는 공중 통제에 대한 전체적인 책임을 맡은 사령관입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.english: The airspace control authority controls the movement of all aircraft.

examples.text: 항공통제권자의 승인을 받아야만 이 지역을 비행할 수 있습니다.
examples.english: You must have the approval of the airspace control authority to fly in this area.

terms.definitionEn: An order implementing the airspace control plan that provides the details of the approved requests for airspace coordinating measures. Also called ACO.
terms.definition: 항공통제명령은 공중 통제 계획을 실행하는 명령으로, 승인된 공중 조정 조치의 세부 사항을 제공합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in written orders and briefings.

examples.english: The airspace control order has been issued to all units.

examples.text: 항공통제명령에 따라 모든 항공기는 지정된 경로로 비행해야 합니다.
examples.english: According to the airspace control order, all aircraft must fly along the designated route.

terms.definitionEn: The document approved by the joint force commander that provides specific planning guidance and procedures for the airspace control system for the joint force operational area. Also called ACP.
terms.definition: 항공통제계획은 합동군 사령관이 승인한 문서로, 합동군 작전 구역을 위한 공중 통제 시스템의 구체적인 계획 지침과 절차를 제공합니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in planning and briefings.

examples.english: The airspace control plan has been approved by the joint force commander.

examples.text: 항공통제계획에 따라 모든 항공기는 정해진 절차를 따라야 합니다.
examples.english: According to the airspace control plan, all aircraft must follow the established procedures.

terms.definitionEn: The planning, coordination, integration, and regulation of airspace by airspace control elements in support of airspace control.
terms.definition: 항공통제관리는 공중 통제 요소가 공중 통제 지원을 위해 공중 공간을 계획, 조정, 통합, 규제하는 것입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in reports and briefings.

examples.text: 항공통제관리는 모든 항공기들의 안전한 운항을 보장합니다.
examples.english: Airspace management ensures the safe operation of all aircraft.
The airspace management team operates 24/7.

terms.definitionEn: A three-dimensional block of airspace in a target area, established by the appropriate commander, in which friendly aircraft are reasonably safe from friendly surface fires. Also called ACA.
terms.definition: 항공통제협조구역은 적대적인 표적 지역에서 우호적인 항공기가 우호적인 지상 화로부터 비교적 안전할 수 있는 공중 공간의 세차원 블록입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports.

examples.text: 항공통제협조구역 내에서는 모든 항공기는 신호기를 사용해야 합니다.
examples.english: All aircraft within the airspace coordination area must use transponders.
The airspace coordination area is safe from enemy threats.

terms.definitionEn: Airspace of defined dimensions within which the ready identification, location, and control of aircraft are required in the interest of security.
terms.definition: ADIZ는 보안상의 이유로 항공기의 신속한 식별, 위치 확인 및 통제가 필요한 정의된 차원의 공중 공간입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in radio communications and reports, formal register.

examples.english: Confirm the aircraft entering the air defense identification zone.

examples.text: 항공식별구역 내에 있는 모든 비행기를 추적하고 있습니다.
examples.english: We are tracking all aircraft within the air defense identification zone.

terms.definitionEn: A restricted air route of travel specified for use by friendly aircraft and established for the purpose of preventing friendly aircraft from being fired on by friendly forces.
terms.definition: 항공통로는 우방 항공기가 우방 세력에 의해 발사되는 것을 방지하기 위해 지정된 제한된 항공 경로입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.english: The air corridor is set from 30,000 feet to 40,000 feet.

examples.text: 항공통로를 사용하는 모든 비행기는 이륙 전에 반드시 승인을 받아야 합니다.
examples.english: All aircraft using the air corridor must obtain approval before taking off.

terms.definitionEn: An airspace coordinating measure that uses altitude to separate users and as the transition between different airspace control elements. Also called CA.
terms.definition: 조정고도는 사용자를 분리하고 다른 항공 공간 제어 요소를 전환하는 데 고도를 사용하는 항공 공간 조율 조치입니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and radio communications.

examples.english: The coordinating altitude is set at 25,000 feet.

examples.text: 모든 항공기는 조정고도에서 다른 항공통제구역으로 이동해야 합니다.
examples.english: All aircraft must transition to another airspace control zone at the coordinating altitude.

terms.definitionEn: Designated areas established by appropriate authority over which flight of aircraft is restricted.
terms.definition: 제한구역은 적절한 권한에 의해 설정된 영역으로, 항공기의 비행이 제한됩니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.

examples.english: All flights are strictly prohibited in the restricted area.

examples.text: 제한구역을 침범한 모든 항공기는 즉시 조치될 것입니다.
examples.english: Any aircraft violating the restricted area will be dealt with immediately.

terms.definitionEn: Airspace designated in an airspace control plan or airspace control order in which there is a concentrated employment of numerous and varied weapons and airspace users. Also called HIDACZ.
terms.definition: 고밀도항공통제구역은 항공 공간 제어 계획 또는 항공 공간 제어 명령에 지정된 영역으로, 다양한 무기 및 항공 공간 사용자가 밀집되어 있습니다. ->
terms.registerNote: Used in briefings and reports.
